# Plan: Auto-Mate (Phase 1 — MVP)

## 1. Overview

Auto-Mate is a self-hostable, AI-powered task automation platform that lets everyday users — not just developers — describe what they need done in plain English, upload files (local or via URL), and get polished results back: cleaned datasets, visualizations, summaries, interactive dashboards, and more. Phase 1 delivers the core automation loop (describe → upload → generate → test → execute → artifacts), persistent task history with reusable task widgets, a task scheduler, and a gamified dashboard. It runs locally with Node.js + Python/uv, or containerized via Docker Compose. Built on pi-web-ui and pi-agent-core for the AI chat interface, with React 19 for the application shell and a composable class-based design system.

**Decomposition Strategy: Vertical Slicing** — Each feature is a thin end-to-end slice (DB → API → UI) delivering user-visible value independently. Features are ordered so each builds on the last, and the app is usable after each slice lands.

## 4. Data Model (High-Level)

### Domain Concepts

- **Task**: A unit of automation. Has a type (`adhoc` or `reusable`), user-provided or AI-derived name, natural language description, and optional parameter schema (for reusable tasks). The organizing entity that all executions, artifacts, and schedules hang off of.
- **Execution**: A single run of a task. Captures the full execution context: input files, generated script (code + language), execution logs (stdout/stderr), status (pending/running/success/failed), timing (start/end/duration), and links to produced artifacts. Immutable once completed.
- **Artifact**: An output file produced by an execution. Has a type (html, csv, pdf, image, markdown, xlsx, plotly-json, etc.), a file path on disk, display metadata (title, description), and a version number. Stored at `~/.automate/artifacts/{taskId}/`.
- **Upload**: A file provided by the user as input to a task. Tracks original filename, detected MIME type, extracted metadata (row count, column names for tabular; page count for docs; dimensions for images), file size, and storage path. Supports both local files and URL-sourced files.
- **Schedule**: A cron/recurrence definition attached to a reusable task. Has a cron expression or simple recurrence (daily/weekly/monthly), next-run timestamp, enabled/disabled state, and links to executions it has triggered.
- **GamificationProfile**: Single-user stats for MVP. Tracks XP, level, current streak (consecutive days with automation), longest streak, achievement flags (bitmask or JSON), and aggregate metrics (total tasks, total artifacts, estimated hours saved).
- **Tool**: A registered automation tool — wraps a sandboxed script (Python or shell) with a parameter schema (TypeBox), an AI-facing description, and execution configuration. Can be built-in or user-created. The AI agent can invoke tools during task execution. Tools are also directly runnable from the UI.
- **Connector**: (Type-only for MVP) An authenticated API wrapper definition. Has a service identifier, auth type (OAuth/API key), configuration schema, and health check interface. No implementations until Phase 2, but the interface exists so Tool definitions can declare connector dependencies.

### Conceptual Relationships

- Task → many Executions (each run produces an Execution record)
- Execution → many Artifacts (each run can produce multiple output files)
- Task → many Uploads (input files/URLs associated with the task)
- Task (reusable) → many Schedules (a reusable task can have multiple schedules)
- Schedule → many Executions (each scheduled run creates an Execution)
- GamificationProfile is a singleton (single-user MVP)
- Tool → invocable by AI agent (via `asAgentTool()`) or user directly

### Storage Strategy

**SQLite** via Drizzle ORM, stored at `~/.automate/data/automate.db`. Chosen because:
- Zero-config, embedded, no external service to manage
- Perfect for single-user local-first deployment
- Drizzle provides type-safe schema definitions and migrations
- libsql compatibility provides optional cloud replication path (Turso) for future
- Handles all persistence needs: task metadata, execution logs, artifact metadata, gamification state, schedule definitions, tool registry, task queue

**File storage** on disk:
- Artifacts: `~/.automate/artifacts/{taskId}/{artifactId}.{ext}`
- Uploads: `~/.automate/uploads/{taskId}/{filename}`
- Generated scripts: `~/.automate/scripts/{executionId}/`
- Python environments: `~/.automate/env/` (shared uv virtualenv, dependencies installed per-task)

**Client-side storage**: pi-web-ui's `IndexedDBStorageBackend` handles chat session persistence (message history, API keys, settings) in the browser. Server-side SQLite handles everything else.

## 5. Interface Design

### Frontend Pages / Views

| Route | Page | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `/` | Dashboard | Gamified home — XP, level, streaks, metrics cards, achievements, recent activity feed, quick-start task button |
| `/task/new` | Task Chat | pi-web-ui ChatPanel embedded in React — primary task creation/execution interface with file upload, AI conversation, real-time progress, artifact preview |
| `/task/:id` | Task Detail | View a specific task — its description, executions, artifacts, and (if reusable) parameter schema + schedule info |
| `/history` | Execution History | Searchable/filterable table of all executions with status, task name, date, duration. Click to view full detail + artifacts |
| `/history/:executionId` | Execution Detail | Full execution view — input files, generated script (expandable), execution logs, produced artifacts (inline preview or download) |
| `/tasks` | Reusable Tasks | Searchable gallery of saved task widgets. Cards showing name, description, last run, run count. Click to re-run or view detail |
| `/scheduler` | Scheduler | Create/edit schedules for reusable tasks. View upcoming scheduled runs. View schedule execution history. Enable/disable toggles |
| `/settings` | Settings | AI provider configuration (wraps pi-web-ui SettingsDialog), sandbox preferences, artifact storage path, gamification toggle, developer mode toggle |

## 6. Security Considerations

Security is built organically into the execution flow, not over-engineered:

- **Script verification loop**: Every AI-generated script passes through ruff (linting) + bandit (security scanning) + AI-generated unit tests + AI code review before execution. Max 3 iteration attempts.
- **Resource limits**: Script execution has configurable timeout (default: 60s) and memory limits. uv virtualenv provides dependency isolation per-task.
- **File access**: Scripts operate on files within the task's designated directories only. The execution environment's working directory is scoped to the task.
- **No outbound network by default**: Generated scripts should not make network calls unless the task explicitly requires it (AI is instructed to flag network usage in the execution plan).
- **Artifact rendering**: pi-web-ui's ArtifactsPanel renders HTML artifacts in sandboxed iframes. Trusted as-is for MVP.
- **User responsibility**: The app provides safety mechanisms, but ultimately the user decides their isolation level. Clear messaging: "For full isolation, run Auto-Mate in a Docker container."
- **Input validation**: All API inputs validated via TypeBox schemas. File uploads validated for MIME type and size (configurable limit, default 50MB).
- **No authentication in MVP**: Single-user local deployment. Auth deferred to Phase 2 (multi-user).

## 7. Architecture & Design (Plan-Specific)

> Standing architecture principles will be established in `.spec-lite/memory.md`.

### Plan-Specific Decisions

- **Server-side AI agent**: pi-agent-core runs on the Express server, not in the browser. The server orchestrates the full task execution loop (analysis → code gen → static analysis → test → review → execute). WebSocket forwards pi-agent-core events to the client for real-time rendering via pi-web-ui components. Rationale: the server must orchestrate Python execution, file I/O, and sandbox management — browser can't do this.

- **pi-web-ui ↔ React integration via refs**: pi-web-ui uses mini-lit web components. React shell wraps them using `useRef` + `useEffect` for lifecycle management. Shared TailwindCSS v4 ensures visual consistency. Rationale: simplest integration path, avoids `@lit/react` build dependency, provides full control over the web component lifecycle.

- **Composable class-based design system**: A design token module in `packages/web` maps semantic classes to TailwindCSS utilities via CSS custom properties. Components use `ds.card`, `ds.btnPrimary`, `ds.surface` etc. — never raw Tailwind classes. CSS variables switch for dark/light mode. This makes the design system extensible (future themes) without touching component code.

- **Task execution as a state machine**: Each execution follows a deterministic state machine: `pending → analyzing → generating → testing → reviewing → executing → completed | failed`. State transitions are logged, and the current state drives the UI progress display. This makes the execution flow predictable and debuggable.

- **Artifact-first output model**: The execution engine is designed around artifact production. Every script execution is expected to produce artifacts (files in a designated output directory). The engine scans the output directory after execution, catalogs artifacts by type, and stores metadata. This is the contract between the AI code generator and the artifact system.

- **Tool interface designed for AI invocability**: Every `Tool` has a TypeBox parameter schema and a natural-language description. The `asAgentTool()` adapter converts it into a pi-agent-core `AgentTool`, making it available in the AI agent's tool list. The AI decides when to invoke tools based on the description. Tools that are not AI-appropriate (dashboard-only widgets) can opt out of the adapter.

- **Execution environment detection**: On startup, the server detects the runtime environment: OS (Windows/macOS/Linux), Python availability (via uv), shell type (PowerShell/bash), and available disk space. This information is injected into the AI's system prompt so generated scripts are platform-appropriate.

## 8. Coding Standards (Plan-Specific Overrides)

> Standing coding standards will be established in `.spec-lite/memory.md`.
> These are plan-specific standards for this project.

- **TypeScript strict mode** everywhere (`strict: true`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true`).
- **No raw Tailwind classes in components** — all styling goes through the design token system.
- **All API endpoints validated** via TypeBox schemas (request body, query params, path params).
- **Server-side code uses ES modules** (ESM) — no CommonJS.
- **Shared types** (Task, Execution, Artifact, Tool, etc.) defined in `packages/core` and imported by both `packages/server` and `packages/web`.
- **File paths use `~/.automate/`** as the root data directory. Configurable via `AUTOMATE_HOME` environment variable.

## 9. Testing Strategy (Plan-Specific)

> Standing testing conventions will be established in `.spec-lite/memory.md`.

- **Unit tests** for `packages/core` — pure logic (file type detection, parameter schema validation, state machine transitions, gamification XP calculations).
- **Integration tests** for `packages/server` — API endpoints with in-memory SQLite, mock AI agent (no real LLM calls), mock script execution.
- **E2E smoke test** — start server, open browser, create a simple task (e.g., "list files in current directory" via shell), verify execution completes and produces output. This validates the full vertical slice.
- **AI-generated script testing** — the execution engine's own test-before-execute loop is the primary quality gate. The engine's test runner is itself tested with known-good and known-bad scripts.
- **Test framework**: Vitest (fast, ESM-native, good TypeScript support, compatible with both Node and browser environments).

## 10. Logging Strategy (Plan-Specific)

> Standing logging conventions will be established in `.spec-lite/memory.md`.

- **Structured JSON logging** on the server (via pino or similar lightweight logger).
- **Execution logs** captured per-execution: AI conversation, generated script, static analysis output, test results, stdout/stderr from execution, timing per phase. Stored in SQLite alongside the execution record.
- **WebSocket event log**: All events sent to the client are also logged server-side for debugging.
- **Client-side**: Console logging for development; no production client logging in MVP.
- **Log levels**: `error` (execution failures, unhandled errors), `warn` (retries, fallbacks), `info` (task lifecycle events), `debug` (AI prompts/responses, script content).
